TASK 4 · ADDITIONAL VERIFIED COMPARISON

Table 4 · CPU utilization category transitions (300-second intervals)

Each row compares two successive observations of the same machine exactly 300 seconds apart. Team E’s transparent CPU thresholds are used: low <20%, medium 20–<40%, high ≥40%. This comparison is distinct from Figure 7’s hourly-mean category proportions.

Transition counts (observations; not percentages)
From → ToLow (<20%)Medium (20–<40%)High (≥40%)Row total
Low44,4928,293052,785
Medium9,49996,0957,631113,225
High88,73411,23019,972

Interpretation: 151,817 of 185,982 valid adjacent comparisons (81.63%) stayed within the same category, while 34,165 (18.37%) changed category. These descriptive changes do not establish task migrations, scheduler actions, or application performance. The 669 intervals longer than 300 seconds, and two adjacent comparisons touching the missing CPU reading, are excluded.

TASK 3 / COMPLETE HANDOVER

Memory utilization & CPU–Memory correlations

48.95%Mean memory utilization (n=187,963)
0.7782Full-pair Pearson r (n=187,962)
0.8608Machine-level Pearson r (1,310 machines)

Member D's workbook reports median memory utilization 51.24%, population SD 13.19 percentage points, and 2.30%–95.42% range. The modal 10-point bin is 50–60% (63,901 observations, 34.00%). Across 187,962 valid CPU–memory pairs, Pearson r = 0.7782 and Spearman ρ = 0.7844.

Using the explicit low <30% / high ≥70% pairwise thresholds, 614 observations (0.327%) have low CPU with high memory, while none have high CPU with low memory. These cutoff choices are for extreme *CPU–memory mismatch* and differ from Team E's preliminary low/mid/high CPU-load categories (<20% / 20–<40% / ≥40%). Neither analysis demonstrates an inefficient cluster scheduler or a degraded application experience.
